newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech, German ministers conclude post-WW2 text.
newsitem.headline: Czech, German ministers conclude post-WW2 text.

text.p: German and Czech Foreign Ministers on Friday signed a protocol ending two years of talks on a joint declaration aiming to put a political wrap on post-World War Two mistrust between neighbours.

The protocol, signed in Prague by German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel and his counterpart Josef Zieleniec, gives preliminary approval to a text expressing Bonn's regret for the 1938-45 Nazi occupation of the Czech lands and Prague's regret for brutality in the post-war expulsion of ethnic Germans.

"We Germans regret the suffering and injustice caused to the Czech people by National-Socialist (Nazi) crimes, and we are recognising our responsibility," Kinkel told diplomats and journalists after signing the protocol. He noted that the text also expresses Czech regret for injustices it committed.

The text, approved by both governments earlier this week, is to be signed by prime ministers in January, but politicians on each side of the border are calling for changes before the parliaments and presidents give their final stamp of approval.
The declaration seeks Germany's final reconciliation with neighbours who fell under Nazi occupation.

But Czech opponents of the text claim it fails to pay direct compensation to victims of Nazi aggression, while German groups are furious that it avoids paying restitution for Prague's post- expropriation of the so-called Sudeten Germans.
